metadata.case_name: LAW SZE CHUN v. LI MIE CHUN

injuries.description: soft tissue injury to the left knee
source: Both experts diagnosed the plaintiff as suffering from soft tissue injury to the left knee.
On examination, it was found that her left knee was swollen with tenderness, abrasion and bruises over it. X-ray of her left knee was unremarkable.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified superficial injury of knee or lower leg

manifestations.description: left knee swollen with tenderness, abrasion and bruises
residual pain in her left knee, particularly on exertion
range of movement of the left knee was reduced, limited by pain
muscle power of the left knee was reduced but with no lower limb muscle wastage detected
cannot walk tip-toe or perform single leg stand with left leg
can now walk in a slow pace with foot dragging and cannot walk for long distances
for the first 6 months after the accident, the plaintiff said she could not walk and has to be wheel-chaired
pain even at night which affects her sleep

treatments_received: attended by the Department of Accident and Emergency of Queen Elizabeth Hospital (QEH)
treated and discharged and referred to QEHs Emergency follow-up clinic
physiotherapy (29 sessions) from 10 December 2013 to 29 April 2014
treatments_future: future medical expenses to cater for pain on a need basis (award HK$10,000)

losses.description: For the first 6 months after the accident, the plaintiff could not walk and had to be wheel-chaired; afterwards she could walk but only very slowly and not for long.

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Tasks of purchasing ingredients for making meals and other shopping, hitherto performed by her, are now taken care of by her son.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Unlike before the accident, she now hardly goes out alone.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: She can no longer enjoy going out to the market to buy food or occasionally going to the park due to difficulty climbing 5 floors of stairs and fear of falling.
